text:
As October rolls around I am once again running my Hacktoberfest {safespace} challenge <https://jcarroll.com.au/2024/10/01/a-safe-space-for-learning-how-to-make-pull-requests/|jcarroll.com.au/2024/10/01/a-safe-space-for-learning-how-to-make-pull-requests>

Anyone new to git/GitHub who would like to try out editing someone else's source code with zero risk that you'll break something important is welcome to submit a pull request (PR) to <https://github.com/jonocarroll/safespace|github.com/jonocarroll/safespace> which I'll review, give feedback about your PR, and guide you through any problems you've encountered with the process. I've merged 10 PRs to that repo and I believe most of the submitters learned something useful in the process - I did, too!

Please share widely for reach, and pass the info on to anyone you know is apprehensively avoiding making their first pull request.

attachments.text:
As October rolls around once more, the term Hacktoberfest might pop across your
feeds; an effort aiming to encourage people to contribute to open-source
software, particularly if they’re new to that. In this post I’ll describe what
I’m offering towards that goal.
